svg.title: The Orchestrator's coordination map
svg.desc: Role and boundary map showing how the Lead orchestrator coordinates the researcher, software engineer, scribe, generalist, and adversarial verifier.
svg.text: Role and boundary map showing how the Lead orchestrator coordinates the researcher, software engineer, scribe, generalist, and adversarial verifier.

text.tspan: Answers one bounded question from primary sources.
Returns a cited briefing a busy engineer can verify and
act on.
Builds the candidate, runs initial checks, performs author
review, and fixes findings assigned by the Lead. Never
owns Git.
Turns verified behavior into documentation inside
assigned targets. Never changes application behavior or
invents release claims.
Owns one self-contained outcome end-to-end when no
specialist fits: discovery, execution, verification, author
review, handoff.

svg.text: Lead of the session · sole owner of the outcome
Delegation transfers an assignment, not accountability.

text.tspan: Record acceptance criteria, scope, constraints, budgets, and material decisions
before work begins.
Stable work items with owner, dependencies, verification, and remaining
corrective-cycle allowance.
Consult the live catalog. Pick the smallest capable soul; resolve fresh versus forked
context.
Inputs, boundaries, owned files, checks, budget, return format, and escalation
conditions.
Separate reported completion from review verdict and from Lead acceptance.
Update the ledger.
Independent review, corrections, final checks, Lead-owned Git/PR/CI, truthful
final response.

svg.text: WORKS DIRECTLY WHEN DELEGATION ADDS OVERHEAD
Small tasks · integration · final checks · Git inspection and publication
Direct work still meets the same acceptance criteria and gates.

text.tspan: Reviews a frozen candidate, not the author's confidence.
Returns one candidate-bound verdict with evidence: PASS,
REVISE, or BLOCKED.
Never edits the deliverable; the Lead routes findings to the
producer.

svg.text: Sets the goal and the authority

text.tspan: Supplies the objective, constraints, and decisions. Authorizes
scope changes and strict-gate exceptions. Receives the plan,
progress, gates, and final result.

svg.text: A specialist recommendation is not user authorization.

text.tspan: Holds the objective, plan, owners, dependencies, evidence, cycles, and
checkpoints. Status is not acceptance: reported completion, review
verdict, and Lead acceptance are tracked separately.

svg.text: Unavailable board → provisional checkpoint; report degraded coordination.
Fork only when inherited history is material.
Every child and result appears in the ledger.
Reported completion is a claim, not acceptance.
20 corrective cycles max; pause on fatal blockers.
Diagram 1 of 3 · Role and boundary map. Arrows show assignment, handoff, review, and durable record flows.
